summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope successfully launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, beginning its transit to Lagrange Point 2 to initiate commissioning for its cosmic mapping mission. In civil space policy and operations, Türkiye signed the Artemis Accords for international space exploration, while NASA brought its new Deep Space Station 23 antenna online at the Goldstone complex to expand the Deep Space Network. NASA also resumed science work on the Swift space telescope following an unsuccessful rescue mission, while NASA and SpaceX delayed their next astronaut launch to the International Space Station due to a leak on the Dragon spacecraft. On the military space front, U.S. Space Force officials reported ongoing struggles to integrate commercial space data, amid global defense updates including Japan's record $55 billion budget request featuring extended-range missiles and Greece's $3.4 billion deal for an Israeli air defense system. Commercial industry updates included the Commercial Space Federation adding two associate members and quantum technology firm Diffraqtion expanding its pre-seed funding round. In scientific developments, researchers identified a massive thermal anomaly beneath the surface of Mars, the James Webb Space Telescope observed a likely early-universe Type II supernova, and laboratory tests demonstrated that peptides can form well-defined structures under Venus-like conditions. Looking ahead, observers should watch Rocket Lab's scheduled early morning launch of a Japanese radar satellite on Sept. 1.
